s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative wound infection with signs of inflammation and necrosis
salient_findings: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
key_facts: 72-year-old man with no prior medical history
Underwent dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
Procedure was for 2:1 atrioventricular block
Discharged on postoperative day 1
Presented with fever on postoperative day 4
Fever was 38.1°C
Lesion over the implant site was inflamed, infiltrating, and necrotic
Laboratory studies revealed an elevated inflammatory syndrome
Blood cultures were obtained
Antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate) were started empirically
Swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
Lesion darkened and enlarged by day 7 despite antibiotic therapy
Blood cultures remained negative by day 7

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal wound infection
shortlist.why_kept: Staphylococcus epidermidis grew from the lesion swab

shortlist.label: Surgical site infection
shortlist.why_kept: Inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy

shortlist.label: Cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory syndrome and signs of inflammation

raw.rationale: The presence of a necrotic lesion over the implant site, which darkened and enlarged despite antibiotic therapy, is highly suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis, a severe infection that causes necrosis of the fascia and surrounding tissues.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal wound infection
rejected.why: While Staphylococcus epidermidis was grown from the lesion, the severity and progression of the lesion suggest a more severe condition than a simple wound infection.

rejected.label: Surgical site infection
rejected.why: This is a broader category that encompasses various types of infections, but the specific details of the case, such as the necrotic nature of the lesion, point towards a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cellulitis
rejected.why: Cellulitis typically presents with erythema, warmth, and swelling, but it does not usually progress to necrosis as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by ulcerative lesions, but it is not typically associated with the acute onset and rapid progression seen in this postoperative setting, nor with positive cultures for Staphylococcus epidermidis.
